#### `CloudCaps`

What a provider can do NATIVELY, as opposed to what the interface's fallbacks emulate. Every operation works on every store; these flags say whether it is cheap.

| Value | Numeric | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `None` | `0` |  |
| `RangeRead` | `1` | The provider can serve a byte range without transferring the whole object (an HTTP Range header, an SDK range option, an FTP restart offset, an SFTP seek). Without it a caller asking for 128 KiB out of a 4 GiB object moves all 4 GiB. |
| `StreamingUpload` | `2` | The provider can consume an upload from a Stream, so a large file is sent in chunks instead of being materialised in memory first. |
| `StreamingDownload` | `4` | The provider can hand back a readable Stream rather than a completed byte[]. |

#### `CloudPath`

Slash-separated path arithmetic for cloud stores: paths never carry a leading slash and the empty string is the root. Mirrors the semantics the pool engine expects so adapters need no re-mapping.

| `GetName` | `static string GetName(string path)` | The last segment of a path ("a/b/c" -> "c"); the empty string for the root. |
| `GetParent` | `static string GetParent(string path)` | The parent of a path ("a/b/c" -> "a/b"); the empty string when already at the root. |

#### `ICloudStore`

The provider-neutral contract every remote endpoint offers: object transfer plus namespace primitives. Each provider implements this directly against its official SDK or REST surface — no meta/wrapper libraries. Paths are slash-separated and never rooted (no leading slash); the empty string is the store root. Implementations translate their native failures into `CloudStorageException` so callers depend on one error model. The streaming and range members carry WORKING default implementations in terms of the whole-object ones, so a provider is correct the moment it implements `Download` and `Upload`. What a provider gains by overriding them is declared in `Caps` — callers use that to decide between a cheap range request and a strategy that assumes whole-object transfers (caching an object once rather than per block).

Implements `IDisposable`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Caps` | `CloudCaps Caps { get; }` | What this provider does natively; the rest is emulated by the defaults below. |
| `Connect` | `void Connect()` | Establishes the connection when the protocol needs one; idempotent. |
| `CreateFolder` | `void CreateFolder(string path)` | Creates one folder level; parents are guaranteed to exist. |
| `DeleteFile` | `void DeleteFile(string path)` |  |
| `DeleteFolder` | `void DeleteFolder(string path)` |  |
| `Download` | `byte[] Download(string path)` | Downloads the whole object; throws `CloudStorageException` with `NotFound` when absent. |
| `List` | `IEnumerable<CloudEntry> List(string folder)` |  |
| `OpenReadRange` | `Stream OpenReadRange(string path, long offset, long count)` | Reads `count` bytes from `offset`. A provider declaring `RangeRead` asks the service for exactly that range; the default has to fetch the whole object and slice it, which is why the capability matters to callers. A range that starts at or past the end yields an empty stream; one that overruns the end is truncated to what exists — the same contract as reading a local file. |
| `OpenRead` | `Stream OpenRead(string path)` | Opens the object for reading as a stream. The default materialises the whole object first; a provider declaring `StreamingDownload` streams it. |
| `Probe` | `bool Probe()` | Cheap reachability check for an online probe; never throws. |
| `Stat` | `CloudMeta Stat(string path)` | File or folder metadata, `null` when nothing exists at the path. |
| `Upload` | `void Upload(string path, Stream content, long length = -1)` | Uploads from a stream, overwriting. The default buffers it into a single array, which caps the object at `MaxValue` and spikes memory by its whole size; a provider declaring `StreamingUpload` sends it in chunks and does neither. |
| `Upload` | `void Upload(string path, byte[] content)` | Uploads the whole object, overwriting; parent folders are guaranteed to exist beforehand. |

#### `SyncBridge`

The one place an asynchronous SDK call is turned into a synchronous one. This library is driven by a filesystem engine whose own callers — WinFsp, Dokan and FUSE — are synchronous callbacks. There is no async path available to propagate, so somewhere the wait has to happen, and doing it in one audited place is better than doing it ad hoc in thirteen providers. The hazard being closed here is the classic one: `task.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` blocks the current thread, and if that thread carries a single-threaded `SynchronizationContext`, the SDK's continuation is posted BACK to it and can never run — the call deadlocks outright rather than merely being slow. The engine normally runs without a context, but "normally" is not a guarantee a storage library should rely on: it is also reachable from the desktop shell and from any host that installs one. So a captured context is escaped before blocking, and the exception is unwrapped so callers see the provider's own `CloudStorageException` instead of an `AggregateException` wrapping it.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Run` | `static T Run<T>(Func<Task<T>> operation)` | Runs an async operation to completion from a synchronous caller. |
| `Run` | `static void Run(Func<Task> operation)` | Runs an async operation with no result to completion from a synchronous caller. |

#### `BearerInjectingHandler`

A delegating handler that stamps a fresh `Authorization: Bearer` header on every outbound request from an `IAccessTokenProvider`. Because the token is fetched per request, a mid-session refresh is picked up transparently by any SDK client built on an `HttpClient` that wraps this handler.

#### `CloudOAuthProviders`

Ready-made `OAuth2Config` factories for the providers this library speaks. Every factory takes the caller's own registered client id (and secret, where the provider mandates one) — nothing is embedded here. Scope defaults grant full read/write on the user's drive and, where the provider gates it behind a flag, offline access so a refresh token is issued.

| Member | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Box` | `static OAuth2Config Box(string clientId, string clientSecret, IReadOnlyList<string> scopes = null)` | Box. Box requires the client secret even for the authorization-code flow. |
| `Dropbox` | `static OAuth2Config Dropbox(string clientId, string clientSecret, IReadOnlyList<string> scopes = null)` | Dropbox. `token_access_type=offline` is what turns a one-shot token into a refreshable one. |
| `GoogleDrive` | `static OAuth2Config GoogleDrive(string clientId, string clientSecret, IReadOnlyList<string> scopes = null)` | Google Drive. Google issues a refresh token only with `access_type=offline` and a fresh consent prompt. |
| `HiDrive` | `static OAuth2Config HiDrive(string clientId, string clientSecret, IReadOnlyList<string> scopes = null)` | Strato HiDrive. Scopes are `{role},{path-scope}`, e.g. `rw,user` for full read/write. |
| `OneDrive` | `static OAuth2Config OneDrive(string clientId, string clientSecret = null, IReadOnlyList<string> scopes = null)` | Microsoft OneDrive — personal and business share the `/common` endpoint; `offline_access` yields the refresh token. |
| `YandexDisk` | `static OAuth2Config YandexDisk(string clientId, string clientSecret, IReadOnlyList<string> scopes = null)` | Yandex Disk (Yandex OAuth). The client secret is required at the token endpoint. |

#### `LoopbackAuthorizer`

Drives the interactive half of the installed-application flow: it opens the provider's consent page in the user's browser and captures the redirect on a transient `http://127.0.0.1:{port}/` loopback listener (the redirect method Google, Microsoft, Box and others bless for native apps). The captured code is exchanged for tokens via `OAuth2Client`. This is the only component that needs a desktop session, so hosts run it once per account and persist the resulting refresh token.

The captured code is exchanged for tokens via `OAuth2Client`. This is the only component that needs a desktop session, so hosts run it once per account and persist the resulting refresh token. |

#### `OAuth2Client`

The transport half of the OAuth2 authorization-code + PKCE flow (RFC 6749 / 7636): builds the authorization URL, exchanges the returned code for tokens, and refreshes an access token from a refresh token. It is deliberately free of any UI or listener — the caller owns redirect capture — so it unit-tests against a stub `HttpClient`.

It is deliberately free of any UI or listener — the caller owns redirect capture — so it unit-tests against a stub `HttpClient`. |

#### `OAuth2TokenProvider`

Keeps a provider's access token fresh: it caches the persisted token set and, when the access token is within the expiry skew, silently refreshes it through the `OAuth2Client` and writes the rotated set back to the `ITokenStore`. A store that holds no refresh token (never authorized, or a token the provider revoked) surfaces as `AccessDenied` so the caller re-runs the login.

Implements `IAccessTokenProvider`.

| Member | Signature | Summary |

A store that holds no refresh token (never authorized, or a token the provider revoked) surfaces as `AccessDenied` so the caller re-runs the login. |
| `GetAccessToken` | `string GetAccessToken()` |  |

#### `PkcePair`

A PKCE (RFC 7636) verifier/challenge pair for the OAuth2 installed-application flow. The verifier is a high-entropy secret kept locally; the challenge is its SHA-256 digest sent on the authorization request, so an intercepted authorization code is useless without the verifier.

Implements `IEquatable<PkcePair>`.

#### `HiDriveCloudStore`

Strato HiDrive store over the HiDrive REST API (`api.hidrive.strato.com/2.1`), authenticated with an OAuth bearer token from the `IAccessTokenProvider`. The service is path-addressed; `rootPath` is the absolute HiDrive base (for example `users/alias`). New files are created with `POST /file` and existing ones replaced with `PUT /file`, matching the API's create-vs-update split.

#### `WebDavCloudStore`

WebDAV store over WebDav.Client (GET/PUT/PROPFIND/MKCOL/DELETE): whole-file, no trusted atomic MOVE, no durable flush. Authenticates with either HTTP Basic credentials or an OAuth bearer token — the latter is how Strato HiDrive and Yandex Disk (over their WebDAV gateways) are reached with a refreshable token.
